name: PiCamera component bench plan
deployment: PiSensor full system deployment, as flown: no test component

event_patterns.piCamera.CaptureCompleted: Capture stored a picture of (?P<bytes>\d+) bytes$
event_patterns.piCamera.AttitudeUnavailable: Attitude unavailable: (?P<reason>\w+) code (?P<code>-?\d+); roll and pitch stored as NaN$
event_patterns.piCamera.TemperatureUnavailable: Temperature unavailable: (?P<reason>\w+) code (?P<code>-?\d+); temperature stored as NaN$
event_patterns.piCamera.LocationUnavailable: Location unavailable: (?P<reason>\w+) code (?P<code>-?\d+); latitude and longitude stored as NaN$

not_covered_ack: METRIC_INVALID (a reading present and fresh but out of range): the bench sensors are not disturbed; unit test InvalidMetric.
Camera failures other than a camera held by another process (NO_CAMERA, TIMEOUT, errors at CONFIGURE, START, FRAME, ENCODE) and TOO_LARGE: unit tests NoCamera, FrameTimeout, CameraErrors, TooLarge.
NO_CONTAINER and BUSY: unit tests NoContainer, BusyDuringCapture.
For each sensor, the path that is not its state on the day (answering or silent): unit tests MetricsCopied, RollPitch, ReadingUnavailable, StaleReading, MissingReading.
coverage.rationale: System coverage is measured over Components/PiCamera of an image built with --coverage, counts copied off the Pi after the plan. The three bench tests run the nominal capture and one camera failure; the failure branches listed are unit-test ground.

REQ-PiCamera-009.note: Response bound CAPTURE_MAX_MS on the target.

REQ-PiCamera-019.note: Capture after the camera is freed.

REQ-PiCamera-024.verification: C-3 (restart after a capture), unit test RecoveryAfterFailure
REQ-PiCamera-024.note: Not verified as written on the bench: the restart of C-3 follows a completed capture, not one in progress (not covered list).

REQ-PiCamera-026.verification: C-1, C-2, C-3 (a capture completes whatever the three sensors do; for each sensor it warns when the window holds no sample of it, and does not warn when its samples are fresh around the capture), unit tests ReadingUnavailable, StaleReading, MissingReading (record content)
REQ-PiCamera-026.note: The bench does not read the stored record. A capture with some samples of a sensor in the window but none fresh around it is not judged for that sensor: channel samples are lost on the downlink, so a gap in the record does not show the unit had no reading.

scope: Bench behaviour of `piCamera` that unit tests cannot show: the real camera, the response time on the target, a camera held by another process, a restart. Product content and downlink are judged by the project plan (`test/int/plan.json`, L2-3 to L2-6).
C-1 and the second half of C-2 and C-3 need a GPS fix: without one every capture fails with `SENSOR_STALE` or `SENSOR_NO_DATA` at `LOCATION` and the tests FAIL.
not_covered: - No camera attached (REQ-PiCamera-016, `NO_CAMERA`): needs the cable removed; unit test `NoCamera`.
- Restart during a capture: the restart of C-3 comes after a completed capture; a capture lasts under 1 s on the bench and the bench action takes longer.

- Content of the `Metrics` record (the three flags, NaN for the values of an unavailable reading): the component plan does not read the product file; unit test `ReadingUnavailable` and the project system tests that read the downlinked product.

tests.title: Capture on the target
tests.purpose: Proves one capture command stores one product through the real camera within the response bound.
tests.setup: Deployment running on the Raspberry Pi 5, camera free, TCP link to the ground workstation up.

tests.title: Camera held by another process, then freed
tests.purpose: Proves a capture fails cleanly while another process holds the camera and succeeds once it is freed.
tests.setup: As C-1. The bench action `camera_hold` starts `rpicam-hello` on the Pi, which opens the camera.

tests.title: Capture after a restart
tests.purpose: Proves the component captures again after the deployment is stopped and started.
tests.setup: As C-1. The bench action `fsw_restart` stops the deployment process on the Pi and starts it again.

rationale.text: The deployment clock is the Pi wall clock, so a restart is no clock restart and the window is not a reset window. The count is since start: 1 after the second capture shows the process restarted between the two captures.
Second witness of the restart: the version events are emitted once at start.
